children: AIRO Group Holdings reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $17.5 million, up 179% year over year, while gross margin rose to 57%. The company recorded a net loss of $12.0 million and Adjusted EBITDA of $(7.5) million. AIRO cited stronger drone sales and reiterated its full-year revenue growth outlook, now expecting results at the lower end of its 15% to 25% range.
Revenue was $17.5 million, up 179% from $6.3 million in the prior-year quarter.
Gross profit was $9.9 million, compared with $2.8 million; gross margin increased to 57% from 44%.
Operating loss was $13.1 million, compared with an operating loss of $12.0 million.
Net loss was $12.0 million, or $0.38 per diluted share, compared with a net loss of $8.0 million, or $0.28 per diluted share.
Adjusted EBITDA was $(7.5) million, compared with $(8.0) million. Cash was $37.8 million and debt was $1.2 million as of September 30, 2026.
Stronger-than-expected growth in the Drones segment drove the quarter’s revenue increase, partially offset by continued softness in Avionics and Training.
AIRO secured its first U.S. order during the quarter and advanced the RQ-70 toward production.
The company reported approximately $200 million in Drone backlog, including U.S. opportunities, as of November 5, 2026, and expects most of it to convert to revenue over the next 12 months.
AIRO’s total opportunity pipeline was approximately $1.5 billion as of November 5, reflecting opportunities across U.S. and allied defense markets.
AIRO reiterated its full-year 2026 Adjusted EBITDA guidance in the negative mid- to high-teens millions range.
